blocks.explanation:
Substitute \(t = \sqrt{x}\) (\(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\)) to get \(2\int e^t(t + 1)\,dt\).
Plan: \(t + 1 = f + f'\) with \(f = t\), so the integral is \(2te^t\); show it by parts.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}(1 + \sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: substitute \(t = \sqrt{x}\); then \(2\int e^t(t + 1)\,dt\), with \(\int te^t\,dt\) by parts.

Parts on \(\int te^t\,dt\)
\[\int te^t\,dt = te^t - \int e^t\,dt = te^t - e^t\]
Why: \(t\) first, \(e^t\) second.

Combine
\[2\int e^t(t + 1)\,dt = 2\left(te^t - e^t + e^t\right) + c\]
\[= 2te^t + c = 2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}} + c\]
Why: \(\int e^t\,dt = e^t\) cancels the \(-e^t\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}}) = \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}} + 2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}(1 + \sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}\]
Why: product and chain rules.
